title: Epimorphy from normalized symmetric Proj sections
statement: For a scheme S and quasi-coherent E, let L be any module on the canonical relative symmetric Proj, with tensor-pullback charts to its degree-one twists, and sigma : E -> p_* L. Suppose each chart sends the tensor-pulled sigma(m) to unitToTwist(iota(m)). Then the tensor-pullback adjoint p^* E -> L is epic. No existence of L, charts or sigma is asserted. The canonical grading and normalization use [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], and [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: The standard opens D_+(iota(m)) cover the symmetric Proj of each affine base chart. Apply Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' and prove algebra generation by SymmetricAlgebra.induction: the degree-zero algebra contains the coefficient scalars and the adjoin contains every iota(m). The canonical grading gives iota(m) degree one.

Use the zero-cancellation criterion for epimorphisms. If f out of L satisfies q followed by f equals zero, naturality of the normalized tensor adjunction identifies sigma followed by p_* f with zero. Thus f annihilates every sigma(m). Naturality of the chart tensor unit and the assumed normalization show that chart.inv followed by j^* f annihilates unitToTwist(iota(m)). Here j^-1(p^-1 U) is the top open, by the relative Proj chart-range formula.

On every open contained in D_+(iota(m)), unitToTwist(iota(m)) is bijective on sections. A morphism out of the structure module is determined by its value on 1, so each composite with this morphism is zero. Lift a twist section through that bijection and evaluate the zero composite to show that the chart morphism vanishes on every smaller open. Since these standard opens cover, sheaf separation proves chart.inv followed by j^* f is zero, hence j^* f is zero.

For an open immersion j, uniqueness of left adjoints compares the tensor-pullback adjunction with the usual module pullback adjunction. The latter unit is bijective on sections of opens contained in j.opensRange, so the tensor unit is injective there. Its naturality therefore detects f=0 on each chart range from j^* f=0. The chart ranges cover the relative Proj; sheaf separation gives f=0 globally and zero-cancellation proves q epic. Empty opens and zero modules require no separate hypotheses.

theorem epi_of_symmetric_twist_sections
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent]
    (L : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj.Modules)
    (chart : ∀ U : S.affineOpens,
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjι U)).obj L ≅
          Proj.twist ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).grading U) 1)
    (σ : E ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
      (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).obj L)
    (hσ :
    ∀ (U : S.affineOpens) (m : E.val.obj (op U.1))
      (hm : SymmetricAlgebra.ι Γ(S, U.1) (E.val.obj (op U.1)) m ∈
        (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).grading U 1),
    (chart U).hom.app
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjι U ⁻¹ᵁ
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))
        (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSection
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjι U) L
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
          (σ.app U.1 m)) =
      Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (Proj.unitToTwist
        (𝒜 := (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).grading U) hm)
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjι U ⁻¹ᵁ
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))
        (1 : Γ(Proj ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).grading U),
          (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjι U ⁻¹ᵁ
            ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)))) :
    Epi (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionAdjunction
      (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom).homEquiv E L).symm σ)
